concept.name: Rolling maximum
concept.definition: The rolling maximum is the highest value of a series within a trailing window of fixed length that slides forward one observation at a time. It underlies channel indicators such as Donchian channels and breakout systems.
concept.intuition: At each point, look back over the last N bars and ask: what was the highest price seen? That level moves as old extremes drop out of the window.
concept.mechanics: For window length w, compute max over observations x_{t−w+1}…x_t and repeat for each t; standard implementations (e.g., pandas rolling().max()) label the result at the window's right edge and return NaN until the window is full unless min_periods is set.
concept.formula: RMax_t = max(x_{t−w+1}, …, x_t), where w is the window length.
concept.failure_modes: The statistic is window-sensitive and jumps discontinuously when an old extreme exits the window, creating artificial 'breakdowns' of the level. Centering the window introduces lookahead bias into backtests.
concept.misconceptions: A break above the rolling maximum is a mechanical event defined by the window choice, not independent evidence of a meaningful breakout.
concept.example: With a 20-day rolling maximum on daily highs, if the highest high of the last 20 days is 112.30, today's upper Donchian line sits at 112.30.
